pending_part_2.voiceover_script: In Part 1, we explored the maddening Taos Hum, the acoustic anomaly that baffled congressional investigators. When acoustic engineers placed the most sensitive seismic detectors across Taos, their equipment recorded absolute silence. The sound did not exist in the air, yet hundreds of people were undeniably hearing it. Medical tests ruled out mass hallucination and tinnitus. Leading neurobiologists now believe the hum is caused by the microwave auditory effect, where ultra-low-frequency electromagnetic radiation directly stimulates the human auditory cortex without creating mechanical sound waves. Declassified naval documents reveal that military very-low-frequency transmitter arrays used to communicate with submerged nuclear submarines blanket the continent in high-power radio waves. Only individuals with unique electromagnetic sensitivity perceive the invisible carrier wave. Could the air around us be vibrating right now?
